pullRequest.title: [all components] Fix stale focused field state

nodes.diff:
Fixes #3987

Disabling or unmounting a focused control can move focus away without firing `blur`, leaving `data-focused` stuck on `Field.Root`, its label, and the control. This is reproducible in Chromium for both native inputs and buttons.

`useSetFieldFocused` records which focus target owns the field state and releases it when that target becomes disabled or unmounts. Ownership prevents cleanup from an old target from clearing focus that has moved to another target, which is required for components with multiple inherent focus targets such as Slider, Radio Group, and OTP Field.

The cleanup is attached to every field-aware focus target: `Field.Control`, `Switch.Root`, `Checkbox.Root`, `NumberField.Input`, `Radio.Root`, `OTPField.Input`, `Slider.Thumb`, `Select.Trigger`, and both `Combobox.Input` and `Combobox.Trigger`.

The PR intentionally stays focused on this lifecycle bug. Filled-state remount handling is already covered on `master`, and uncommon compositions with multiple independent controls under one `Field.Root` are left unsupported rather than adding runtime coordination.

Fixes #3987

Two Field lifecycle states could go stale, both because the control that owned the state never got to release it.

**`filled` across control replacement.** A filled uncontrolled control replaced by a fresh empty one under the same `Field.Root` kept `data-filled`. It now follows last-attach-wins ownership of the shared input ref: the owner publishes unconditionally on attach, a superseded control can't clear its successor's state, and a survivor reclaims a null ref after the owner unmounts. Form registration reads the control's own element rather than the mutable shared ref, so field values stay readable when control lifetimes overlap.

**`focused` on disable and unmount.** Every control cleared the field's focused state only in `onBlur`, but two paths drop focus without firing blur: disabling a focused control, and unmounting one. Either left `data-focused` stuck on `Field.Root`, the label, and the control. Confirmed in Chromium: re-rendering a focused `<input>` or `<button>` as disabled moves focus to `<body>` and fires no blur event at all.

The new `useSetFieldFocused` hook returns the field's `setFocused` and clears it in a layout effect on both paths. Every control that reports focus now uses it: `Field.Control`, `Switch.Root`, `Checkbox.Root`, `NumberField.Input`, `OTPField.Root`, `RadioGroup`, `Slider.Thumb`, `Select.Trigger`, and both `Combobox.Input` and `Combobox.Trigger`. `OTPField.Root` also keeps a separate local focused state, which is cleared alongside it.

A field can own several controls, so the hook records which control the focused state belongs to, and only that control clears it. Ownership has to live on the field rather than in a per-control flag: `Slider.Thumb` deliberately skips its blur handling when focus moves to a sibling thumb, which leaves a per-control flag stale, and disabling that thumb would then clear focus belonging to its sibling.

Native label association is deliberately left on the existing commit-driven lifecycle (tests now pin it, including labels in other containers, `htmlFor` retargeting, and OTP slots mounting late). Label changes with no control rerender at all remain untracked in v1: `useAriaLabelledBy` patches over the hidden-input-inside-label layout, which is slated for rework in v2, and observer-based tracking measurably regressed mount performance for what it covered.

Two Field lifecycle states could go stale across control replacement. A filled uncontrolled control replaced by a fresh empty one under the same `Field.Root` kept `data-filled` set, and a control removed while focused never fires blur, leaving `data-focused` stuck on the root.

`filled` now follows last-attach-wins ownership of the shared input ref: the owning control publishes unconditionally on attach, a superseded control can't clear its successor's state, and a survivor reclaims a null ref after the owner unmounts. Each control also tracks whether it holds the field's focused state and releases it on unmount only in that case. Form registration reads the control's own element rather than the mutable shared ref, so field values stay readable when overlapping control lifetimes clear that ref.

Label changes with no control rerender at all remain untracked in v1: `useAriaLabelledBy` patches over the hidden-input-inside-label layout, which is slated for rework in v2, and observer-based tracking measurably regressed mount performance for what it covered.

Three Field lifecycle states could go stale because they were only recomputed when the control itself committed. A native `<label>` rendered independently could mount, unmount, or retarget without the control rerendering, leaving `aria-labelledby` pointing at a removed element (or never forming). A filled uncontrolled control replaced by a fresh empty one under the same `Field.Root` kept `data-filled` set. A focused control removed without firing blur left `data-focused` stuck on the root.

Label association now re-syncs on every commit and through a per-control `MutationObserver` watching the label source's parent, so both rerender-driven and fully independent label changes are covered without observing the whole document. This applies to Checkbox, Switch, Radio, and OTP Field via the shared `useAriaLabelledBy` hook.

For `filled`, ownership follows the shared input ref: the last control to attach owns publishing, a superseded control can no longer clear the active control's state, and a surviving control reclaims a null ref after the owner unmounts. For `focused`, each control tracks whether it holds the field's focused state and releases it on unmount only in that case, so a blurred control never clears state owned by its successor.
